name: Warrant
comment: NOTE FOR FUTURE MAINTAINERS/AGENTS: some patterns in this grammar highlight CROSS-SCHEMA REFERENCE syntax that is a DESIGN PROPOSAL and NOT YET IMPLEMENTED in the Warrant DSL parser. The proposed form is KEYWORD(<predicate> for <handle> [with <context map>]) — e.g. can(create_timesheet for users(@context user_id)) and check(is_open('p') for pay_periods(@context id) with k = @context v). Forward-looking pieces: the `can(...)`/`check(...)` builtins used in expression position, the `for` and `with` keywords, `[ ]` ability lists, the `any`/`of` keywords, the `=` operator, and the `entity.name.namespace` scope on a schema handle after `for`. See ./FUTURE-FEATURES-cross-schema-references.md (next to this file) for the full plan. If those features are cut or their syntax changes, update or remove the patterns tagged 'FUTURE:' below.

schema-target.comment: FUTURE: `for <schema-handle>` inside a cross-schema can(...)/check(...). Highlights `for` as a keyword and the schema name that follows it as a namespace. The optional row-binding `(@context id)` after the name is tokenized by the other rules. Same-line only (a match cannot span lines); when `for` and the handle are on different lines, `for` falls back to the keyword rule below. Not yet supported by the parser.

keywords.comment: if/they/can/cannot/and/or/not are current keywords. FUTURE: check/for/with/any/of are cross-schema keywords (see file header note). `can`/`check` also act as expression-position builtins; they still scope as keywords here.
keywords.name: keyword.control.warrant

operators.comment: ! * ? are current operators. FUTURE: `=` is the assignment in a `with key = value` context-mapping clause.
operators.name: keyword.operator.warrant

punctuation.comment: ( ) , are current punctuation. FUTURE: [ ] delimit an ability list in a cross-schema can(...).
punctuation.name: punctuation.separator.warrant
